output_list.criticism: The increaseApproval function is vulnerable to integer overflow. An attacker can increase the value of the contract for a specific user by calling this function with a large input value. This can lead to the contract balance being increased beyond the maximum representable value, resulting in incorrect calculations and potentially loss of funds.

The decreaseApproval function is also vulnerable to integer overflow. An attacker can decrease the value of the contract for a specific user by calling this function with a large input value. This can lead to the contract balance being decreased beyond the maximum representable value, resulting in incorrect calculations and potentially loss of funds.

The mint function is vulnerable to integer overflow. The owner can set the balance of an arbitrary user to any value by calling this function with a large input value. This can lead to the contract balance being increased beyond the maximum representable value, resulting in incorrect calculations and potentially loss of funds.

The pullBack function is vulnerable to integer overflow. The owner can retrieve a specific amount of tokens from the contract by calling this function with a large input value. This can lead to the contract balance being decreased beyond the maximum representable value, resulting in incorrect calculations and potentially loss of funds.

The showMyTokenBalance function is vulnerable to integer overflow. The owner can display the balance of a specific user by calling this function with a large input value. This can lead to the contract balance being incorrectly calculated, potentially leading to incorrect user balances.
